sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
The path was not smooth: revenue grew 1.4% in FY2021, then 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024 before slowing to 2.8% in FY2025 [D129][D179][D202][D226].

The FY2023 step change came from higher rates lifting net interest income, which rose 33.8% that year [D174], with deposit margin expansion on higher rates cited across the payments and commercial businesses [P37][P50].
FY2025's slowdown reflects deposit margin compression and lower rates, which offset higher Markets net interest income and revolving Card balances [P28].
North America remains the core at 76.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only +0.2pp of growth that year, against +20.6pp in FY2023 [D249][D251][D245].
International markets carried FY2025: EMEA grew 9.5% and Asia-Pacific 17.3%, contributing +1.2pp each [D275][D276][D300][D301].
Loan growth of $121.1 billion was predominantly driven by higher CIB loans, primarily in Markets, and higher securities-based lending in AWM on client demand [P4].
Net income grew 9.7% a year against 6.2% for noninterest income and 8.4% for net interest income, while diluted EPS compounded at 13.9% as the share count fell [F113][F112][F111][F115].
Noninterest expense grew 4.2% in FY2025 against 2.8% revenue growth, so the incremental margin was negative that year [D225][D226].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, better than the 57.2% window median and near the 51.7% window low of FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
Noninterest expense rose to $95.6 billion on higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing investment [X137][P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 from 6.0% in FY2024, above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].

The higher provision reflected net increases in the loan and commitment portfolios, credit-quality changes on client-specific exposures and estimated losses on borrower fraud in secured lending facilities [P15].
Net margin held at 31.2% against a 21.4% effective tax rate, so the provision, not tax, explains the gap to operating profitability [D210][D203].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was negative $147.8 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The outflow resulted from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations and purchases, and higher other assets, partly offset by net income [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion in FY2025 were 84.6% of net income [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, at the 100th percentile of the seven-bank peer group against an 11.8% median [D213][D338][D339].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 43.1% in FY2021 as deposit growth outran lending through the pandemic [D211][D115].
The firm held $343 billion of cash and equivalents at FY2025, down 26.8% year over year, alongside $449 billion of available FHLB and discount-window borrowing capacity [F100][D219][P9].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion in FY2025 helped cut the diluted share count 3.4% [X102][X112][D224].

Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10%; the 10-K figure for FY2025 is $57.0 billion [R1][X20][F30].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion, about 3.4% of wholesale credit exposure, from $44.7 billion, driven by downgrades and new commitments [P2].
Nonaccrual loan exposure increased $273 million, driven by downgrades in Technology, Media & Telecommunications, Utilities, Central Government and Oil & Gas [P1].
The FY2020 pretax income and tax figures were later restated, so comparisons using those lines carry a small basis difference [R2][R3].
If the efficiency ratio moves back above the 57.2% window median from 52.4%, the cost discipline behind the margin story would be reversing [D207][D333].
A credit-loss provision above the FY2025 level of 7.8% of revenue would confirm the rising-criticized-exposure trend [D208][P2].
Net interest income growth below the FY2025 rate of 3.1% would signal that deposit margin compression is outpacing loan growth [D221][P28].
